title: waybill repo observation report
description: A machine-readable account of what waybill saw, claimed, ignored, and could not determine while traversing a repository. ALPHA: additive change is expected; see schema_version.

schema_version.description: Two-part version. Minor increments for additive change (a new field, a new enum member); major for a removal, a rename, or a change to an existing field's type or meaning. A consumer meeting an unrecognised major MUST refuse to interpret the report.

schema_stability.description: Stability of this schema. `alpha` means consumers must tolerate new fields and new enum members without breaking.

volatile_fields.description: Self-describing list of the fields that legitimately differ between two runs over an unchanged repository. A differ masks exactly these and needs no out-of-band knowledge, so it stays correct as the schema grows.

redaction_mode.description: `none` retains repository-relative path segments; `paths` replaces each with a stable identifier. Absolute paths and file contents are absent in BOTH modes.

significance_threshold.description: Unclaimed-file count above which an otherwise-unremarkable directory earned its own record. Two reports produced under different thresholds are NOT comparable; a consumer diffing them must check this first.

totals.description: Repository-wide counts. INVARIANT: files_walked == files_claimed + files_unclaimed + sum(files_skipped). A report violating it is invalid and may be rejected outright.

files_skipped.description: Skip counts by reason. Reasons are enumerated rather than collapsed into a single 'other' bucket -- an 'other' bucket is where a census stops being checkable.

components_emitted.description: Components credited to this reader, derived by sole-claimant attribution. `null` means NOT DETERMINED -- never 'produced nothing'. A reader with files_matched > 0 and components_emitted == 0 engaged and produced nothing, which is a different diagnosis from a reader that never matched.

path.description: Repository-relative. Never absolute, in any mode.

claim_status.description: EXCLUSIVE. Exactly one applies. Note what is absent: there is no `indeterminate` -- ambiguity is a separate, independent field, because a directory can be claimed AND ambiguous.

claimed_by.description: Non-empty exactly when claim_status is `claimed`. Readers whose patterns match everything are content probes, not claimants, and never appear here.

files_aggregated.description: Rolled up from descendants that earned no record of their own. Kept separate from files_direct so aggregation preserves counts without pretending the files live here.

evidence_marker.description: The marker FILE that produced this attribution. Attribution is marker-driven; source-file extensions alone never produce one, because a directory's marker often sits above the source it governs.

ambiguity.description: Independent of claim_status. Its presence never changes what claim_status says, and a consumer MUST NOT infer absence of ambiguity from a `claimed` status.

interpretations.description: Competing readings, NEVER ranked. At least two: a single interpretation is a classification and belongs in `ecosystems` instead.

evidence.description: What was observed that produced the ambiguity, so a reader can evaluate the call rather than trust it.

observation.description: Present when the directory is not confidently classified -- defined as: at least one ecosystem attribution AND no ambiguity record.

extension_histogram.description: Observation only. MUST NOT drive an ecosystem attribution.

content_kind.description: A heuristic over a sampled prefix, reported as such. 47 binary files and 47 text files are both unclassified and mean entirely different things.

content_sample_bytes.description: Bytes sampled per file. Present so a reader knows the verdict came from a prefix, not the whole file.
